The traditional HTTP\-FLV live stream solution (that is, [Pulling FLV streams](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/docs-flv-streaming-integration)) typically has a latency of around 5 seconds, which affects the viewers' real\-time interaction experience and causes viewers to see exciting moments with a delay. To address this issue, BytePlus MediaLive Player SDK for Web provides a low\-latency FLV live stream solution. This solution can reduce **live stream latency to 2\-3 seconds**, and supports dynamic switching between 3\-5 quality levels. While ensuring low latency, it effectively reduces the video stuttering rate in poor network conditions. This topic will guide you to quickly integrate this solution, bringing your viewers a lower latency and smooth real\-time viewing experience.

<span id="185ce4d3"></span>
# Applicable scenarios

If you are building live stream scenarios with high real\-time requirements, this solution is your ideal choice:


* **Sports live streaming**: For example, football, esports, and other large\-scale competitive events, enabling viewers to watch in sync with the live event.

* **Enterprise press conference**: For example, media coverage, new product launches, and more, ensuring information reaches viewers instantly.

* **Large\-scale gala**: For example, New Year's Eve galas, corporate annual meetings, creating an immersive experience.

* **General entertainment live streaming**: Meeting various interactive web live stream playback needs.


<span id="eb7ead5c"></span>
# Solution advantages

After integrating this solution, your live streaming app will gain the following core advantages:


* **Ultra\-low latency, latency as low as 2\-3 seconds**: By optimizing the Group of Pictures (GOP) caching strategy, using frame pushing, zero\-buffer transmission, and player dynamic frame chasing technology, live stream latency is significantly reduced from around 5 seconds.

* **Anti\-stuttering in poor networks, video stuttering rate reduced by over 30%** : The solution features built\-in adaptive bitrate (ABR) technology, supporting dynamic switching between 3–5 quality levels. The player automatically adjusts the quality level based on viewers' network conditions. When the network is poor, it switches to a lower bitrate to ensure smooth playback, and when the network recovers, it switches back to a higher bitrate to ensure video quality.


<span id="b811078b"></span>
# Core principle: Why does your live stream have latency?

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

To understand how this solution reduces latency to 2 seconds, you first need to understand how live stream latency is generated. Among these, the time consumed by host\-side push streaming and the content delivery chain is relatively fixed, while **Content Delivery Network (CDN) node caching** and **playback\-side buffering** are two key bottlenecks that cause latency and can be optimized.


1. **Host\-side push streaming**: Refers to the process of video capturing, encoding, packaging, and pushing to CDN nodes. The latency in this stage is affected by device performance, upstream network, GOP (keyframe interval) size, and other factors, and typically accounts for a small proportion and offers limited room for optimization.

2. **Content delivery chain**: Refers to the path through which the video stream is transmitted via CDN global nodes. Although BytePlus MediaLive CDN adopts an 'immediate forwarding upon receipt' strategy, data still incurs approximately 100 milliseconds of transmission latency each time it passes through a node (one hop) in the network.

3. **CDN node caching (key latency bottleneck)** : To ensure a fast startup and a smooth viewing experience, CDN nodes cache a segment of video content for a period of time (usually one or more GOPs). When viewers request playback, the CDN transmits data starting from the most recent cached keyframe (I\-frame). This **caching duration** serves as the base latency and is directly added to the total latency perceived by viewers.

4. **Playback\-side buffering (key latency bottleneck)** : To cope with viewers' network fluctuations and avoid frequent stuttering, the player preloads and maintains a safe buffer. The **size of this buffer** directly affects the gap between what viewers see and the live event.


<span id="630a478d"></span>
# Core features

<span id="05db368b"></span>
## Average live stream latency reduced to 2 seconds, synchronizing viewers with the live event

<video src="https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/78d61ef4fa7a40899d52549b593b8305~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image" controls></video>



* **Faster playback startup**: The GOP caching strategy for CDN nodes has been optimized, allowing viewers to load the video more quickly after clicking play.

* **Consistent low\-latency state**: Dynamic buffer adjustment and accelerated frame chasing mechanism have been introduced for the player. Even during playback, the buffer size can be dynamically adjusted to always keep the viewers' video in a low\-latency state.


<span id="85a38ee2"></span>
## ABR technology: Smart switching between quality levels to balance smooth playback and video quality

</Tab>
<Tab zoneid="ivPKcoj5IJ" title="After the ABR feature is enabled">
<TabTitle>After the ABR feature is enabled</TabTitle>

<video src="https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/1998e0a0facd48e79776fa59f50e14df~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image" controls></video>



</Tab>
</Tabs>


In low\-latency scenarios, fluctuations in the viewers' network can easily cause video stuttering. To address this issue, BytePlus MediaLive provides ABR technology. This technology ensures low latency while automatically balancing smooth playback and video quality according to viewers' network conditions.

You can configure 3–5 different quality levels, such as Ultra\-High Definition (UHD), High Definition (HD), and Standard Definition (SD). The player will monitor viewers' network conditions in real time and automatically switch seamlessly between these levels:


* **When a viewer's network is poor**: Automatically switch to a quality level with lower bitrate, sacrificing some video quality to ensure smooth playback.

* **When a viewer's network recovers**: Automatically switch back to a quality level with higher bitrate to present better video quality.


The entire switching process not only reduces the video stuttering rate in poor network conditions by more than 30%, but also consistently maintains 2–3 seconds of low latency, providing your viewers with a smooth and high\-definition viewing experience.

<span id="a36c7a79"></span>
## No release required, dynamically optimize online playback performance

In addition to the preset standard configuration, to further optimize the viewing experience according to real\-time playback performance, you can [contact MediaLive technical support](https://console.byteplus.com/workorder/create) at any time to adjust playback strategies for you. The entire process **does not require you to modify code or release a new version**, allowing you to respond quickly and flexibly to business changes.

The key dimensions you can dynamically adjust include:


* **Low latency mode**: Enable or disable low latency mode as needed based on the importance of the live streaming content, such as key events or interactive live streaming.

* **Caching strategy**: Fine\-tune the caching strategy to find the optimal balance for your business between live stream latency and smooth playback.

* **Bitrate switching sensitivity**: Flexibly adjust the strategy to balance video quality and smooth playback according to your business scenario. By dynamically adjusting this strategy, you can provide viewers with the optimal viewing experience in different live stream scenarios, even under complex network conditions.

   * **Prioritize smooth playback**: In highly interactive live streams, you can configure the player to quickly switch to a quality level with lower bitrate during network fluctuations, minimizing stuttering and ensuring a smooth interactive experience.

   * **Prioritize video quality**: In live streams with high video quality requirements, you can configure the player to maintain high bitrate playback as much as possible, delivering a good visual experience.


Dynamic configuration enables your playback strategy to quickly respond to online changes, achieving dynamic optimization for key metrics such as latency control and smooth playback, thereby providing viewers with a more stable and higher\-quality live stream viewing experience.

# Integration steps

<span id="6b176349"></span>
## Step 1: Add the ABR configuration in the console

To implement the ABR feature, you need to configure transcoding at multiple quality levels for the source stream in the console.


1. Log in to the [BytePlus MediaLive console](https://console.byteplus.com/live).

2. In the left\-side navigation pane, select **Feature configuration** and click the **Adaptive bitrate** tab on the right.

3. Select your desired domain name space from the **Domain name space** drop\-down list and then click **Add configuration**.

4. In the dialog box that appears:

   1. Enter the `AppName` from your push stream address. For example, if the push stream address is `rtmp://push.example.com/live/test?authinfo`, then the `AppName` is `live`.

   2. Add substreams with quality levels of UHD, HD, SD, and LD.

   You can keep the other configurations in their default settings. For more information, see [Managing adaptive bitrate configuration](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/docs-configuring-an-hls-abr-task).

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/85e4c93d717348bc833e252afc75eded~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>


<span id="71e9acef"></span>
## Step 2: Get FLV pull stream addresses for different quality levels

After adding the ABR configuration, you need to generate a dedicated FLV pull stream address for each quality level.


1. Log in to the [BytePlus MediaLive console](https://console.byteplus.com/live).

2. In the left\-side navigation pane, click **Address generator**.

3. Complete the following configurations, click **Generates Pull stream address**, and get the FLV pull stream address for a specific quality level on the right.

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/795e50db176d41db8d3a03069538a2c4~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

   * **Address type**: Select **Pull stream address**.

   * **Domain name**: Select the domain name for stream pulling within the domain name space used when adding the ABR configuration.

   * **AppName** and **StreamName**: Use your push stream address to determine the values for these fields. If your push stream address is `rtmp://push.example.com/live/test?authinfo`:

      * **AppName**: The `AppName` is the part of the address after the domain. In this case, you would enter `live`.

      * **StreamName**: First, identify the **base stream name** from the address, which is `test`. Then, for each quality level, append the corresponding substream suffix to this base name. For example:

         * For the UHD quality level, enter `test_uhd`

         * For the HD quality level, enter `test_hd`

   Repeat this step to generate and record the FLV pull stream address for each quality level.


**Example**

The following table lists examples of FLV pull stream addresses and corresponding bitrate values for different quality levels.


|Quality level |FLV pull stream address |Bitrate (kbps) |
|---|---|---|
|UHD |https://pull.example.com/live/123456_uhd.flv |3200 |
|HD |https://pull.example.com/live/123456_hd.flv |2048 |
|SD |https://pull.example.com/live/123456_sd.flv |1638 |
|Low Definition (LD) |https://pull.example.com/live/123456_ld.flv |1024 |


<span id="4fd58690"></span>
## Step 3: Integrate the Player SDK for Web

Integrate version 2.11.0 or above of the Player SDK for Web into your project. For more information, see [Integrating the Player SDK for Web](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/docs-integrating-the-player-sdk-for-web_1).

If you use the NPM method to import dependencies, you must import and register the `flv` and `abr` plugins to ensure that low\-latency FLV and ABR features are available. The sample code is as follows.

```JavaScript
import { flv, abr } from '@byteplus/veplayer-plugin'
register([flv, abr]);
```


Since some mobile browsers (such as Safari before iOS 16) cannot play FLV streams, to ensure that the live stream can still play normally on these devices, the SDK provides an HLS fallback solution. After enabling this solution, when the player detects that the current browser does not support playing FLV streams, it will automatically switch to the alternative HLS stream for playback. To ensure that the fallback works properly, if you import dependencies via NPM, be sure to also import and register the `hlsjs` plugin. The sample code is as follows.

```JavaScript
import { flv, hlsjs, abr } from '@byteplus/veplayer-plugin';
register([flv, hlsjs, abr]);
```


<span id="d64fecdd"></span>
## Step 4: Configure ABR and enable low\-latency FLV in the SDK

When creating the player, you can use the following configurations to provide viewers with a low\-latency, smooth, and fully platform\-compatible live streaming experience:


* **Configure ABR feature**: The ABR feature is enabled by default in the SDK. You only need to provide a list containing multiple bitrates and their corresponding FLV pull stream addresses. The player will automatically switch quality levels during the live stream based on viewers' network conditions, ensuring smooth playback while providing good video quality.

* **Listen** **for quality level switch events**: To implement custom logic when switching quality levels, such as updating the UI or reporting switch data, you can listen for the following events:

   * `ABR_SWITCH_START`: Start switching the quality level.

   * `ABR_SWITCH_SUCCESS`: The quality level was switched successfully.

   * `ABR_SWITCH_FAILED`: Quality level switching failed.

* **Mobile HLS fallback solution**: Some mobile browsers (such as Safari before iOS 16) do not support playing FLV streams. To ensure that the live stream can play normally on these devices, you can provide a backup HLS pull stream address when configuring the FLV pull stream addresses. When the player detects that the current browser does not support playing FLV streams, it will automatically switch to the HLS stream for playback.


The sample code is as follows.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">To ensure that the ABR feature works properly, make sure that the bitrate you set for each quality level in the code matches that of the ABR configuration in the console.</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning"><strong>Please pay special attention to unit conversion:</strong></div>



* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning"><strong>Bitrate unit in the console:</strong> <code>kbps</code></div>


* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning"><strong>Bitrate unit in the code:</strong> <code>bps</code></div>



<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">Therefore, the bitrate value set in the code must be <strong>1000</strong> times the value in the console.</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">For example, if the console is set to <code>3200</code> kbps, then <code>3200000</code> should be passed in the code.</div>



<Tabs>
<Tab zoneid="xJBbB6mtk2" title="CDN">
<TabTitle>CDN</TabTitle>

```JavaScript
VePlayer.createLivePlayer({
    width: 640,
    height: 360,
    playlist: [
      {
        definitions: [
          // FLV pull stream address for the initial playback quality level.
          'https://pull.example.com/live/123456_uhd.flv',
          // HLS pull stream address for fallback playback, which can be generated through the console's address generator.
          'https://pull.example.com/live/123456_uhd.m3u8',
        ],
      },
    ],
    flv: {
      abr: {
        // Bitrate for the initial playback quality level. Unit is bps.
        bitrate: 3200000,
        // Bitrates and FLV pull stream addresses for each quality level. Bitrate unit is bps.
        urls: {
          3200000: 'https://pull.example.com/live/123456_uhd.flv',
          2048000: 'https://pull.example.com/live/123456_hd.flv',
          1638000: 'https://pull.example.com/live/123456_sd.flv',
          1024000: 'https://pull.example.com/live/123456_ld.flv',
         }
     }
  },
    fallback: {
      // Try to play the low-latency FLV stream first. When the player detects that the current browser cannot play the low-latency FLV stream, it will automatically fallback to HLS stream for playback. 
      fallbackOrder: ['ll-flv', 'hls'],
    }
}).then(function (veplayer) {
    // Listen for quality level switching events.
    veplayer.on(VePlayer.live.Events.ABR_SWITCH_START, function (data) {
      console.log('ABR_SWITCH_START', data.bitrate);
    });

    veplayer.on(VePlayer.live.Events.ABR_SWITCH_SUCCESS, function (data) {
      console.log('ABR_SWITCH_SUCCESS', data.bitrate);
    });

    veplayer.on(VePlayer.live.Events.ABR_SWITCH_FAILED, function (data) {
      console.log('ABR_SWITCH_FAILED', data.bitrate);
    });
})
```

```JavaScript
import { createLivePlayer, register, live } from '@byteplus/veplayer';
import { flv, hlsjs, abr } from '@byteplus/veplayer-plugin';
import '@byteplus/veplayer/style'

register([flv, hlsjs, abr]);

createLivePlayer({
    width: 640,
    height: 360,
    playlist: [
      {
        definitions: [
           // FLV pull stream address for the initial playback quality level.
          'https://pull.example.com/live/123456_uhd.flv',
          // HLS pull stream address for fallback playback, which can be generated through the console's address generator.
          'https://pull.example.com/live/123456_uhd.m3u8',
        ],
      },
    ],
    flv: {
      abr: {
        // Bitrate for the initial playback quality level. Unit is bps.
        bitrate: 3200000,
        // Bitrates and FLV pull stream addresses for each quality level. Bitrate unit is bps.
        urls: {
          3200000: 'https://pull.example.com/live/123456_uhd.flv',
          2048000: 'https://pull.example.com/live/123456_hd.flv',
          1638000: 'https://pull.example.com/live/123456_sd.flv',
          1024000: 'https://pull.example.com/live/123456_ld.flv',
      }
    }
  },
    fallback: {
      // Try to play the low-latency FLV stream first. When the player detects that the current browser cannot play the low-latency FLV stream, it will automatically fallback to HLS stream for playback. 
      fallbackOrder: ['ll-flv', 'hls'],
    }
}).then(function (veplayer) {
    // Listen for quality level switching events.
    veplayer.on(live.Events.ABR_SWITCH_START, function (data) {
      console.log('ABR_SWITCH_START', data.bitrate);
    });

    veplayer.on(live.Events.ABR_SWITCH_SUCCESS, function (data) {
      console.log('ABR_SWITCH_SUCCESS', data.bitrate);
    });

    veplayer.on(live.Events.ABR_SWITCH_FAILED, function (data) {
      console.log('ABR_SWITCH_FAILED', data.bitrate);
    });
})
```
